judgmentCalls: task 1: M4's upper bound (<=70) is tighter than the subject rule alone yields. Applying only the Context's stated subject test (delete marker-edge / Depends-on / text-dependency / cycle-from-markers / marker-placement / near-miss-marker / heuristic-classification tests plus the Commutes: section, keep everything the 'stays' list names) leaves 82 collected cases, which fails M4. To land at 68 I additionally dropped 14 cases that are near-duplicate coverage inside a kept subject, keeping the stronger pin of each pair: test_mixed_case_attr_ref_still_dropped_from_files and test_dotted_attribute_ref_is_not_a_write (test_extensionless_real_files_are_kept_identifiers_dropped already pins `schema.User` is dropped), test_bare_none_files_entry_is_silent (test_bulleted_none_in_files_is_not_a_conflict), test_canonical_files_block_compiles_clean, test_placeholder_interfaces_emit_no_undeclared_dependency and test_all_three_tasks_share_wave_one (same PLACEHOLDER_PLAN family as the M3-named test), test_symbol_lead_with_prose_tail_still_tokens (test_placeholder_token_set), test_emit_launch_is_opt_in, test_v5_plan_compiles_clean_with_empty_interface_defaults, test_unmarked_task_emits_lean_review_slot, test_implementation_files_noise_still_blocks_compile, test_section_titles_with_task_word_stay_legal (test_prose_section_heading_with_task_word_and_colon_compiles), plus test_files_less_heuristic_task_is_exempt and test_markerless_files_noise_still_blocks_compile, whose subject is the markerless/heuristic branch the claims-v1 grammar has no tasks for. The Context's own estimate was 45-60 survivors, so this is the direction it expected; naming it here because it is a judgment cull rather than a pure subject cull.
